purpose.purpose: A reliable prioritized in-memory task queue engine supporting FIFO/priority scheduling, task leasing, TTL expiration, deterministic state snapshots, and JSON serialization/deserialization.
purpose.problemStatement: Problem addressed by aidm-pilot-task-queue: deliver a reliable prioritized in-memory task queue engine supporting fifo/priority scheduling, task leasing, ttl expiration, deterministic state snapshots, and json serialization/deserialization.
purpose.desiredOutcome: A small, real, independently versioned TypeScript project implementing a reliable in-memory task queue library with comprehensive automated test coverage.
purpose.measurableObjective: Automated test suite passing with zero regressions

primaryUsers: Developers and software systems requiring a prioritized in-memory task queue engine with leasing and snapshot determinism
externalActors: External Service (Consumable as an independent TypeScript module / library)

capabilities: Domain models: TaskItem, TaskPriority, QueueConfig, TaskLease
Persistence representation: deterministic JSON state serialization, JSON deserialization, schema validation
Queue operations: enqueue, dequeue, peek, lease, release, expireStale
Verification: unit tests, integration/E2E tests, build/typecheck verification
workflows: State Serialization and Deserialization Round-trip with Schema Validation
integrations: Consumable as an independent TypeScript module / library

functionalRequirements.title: Core Functionality
functionalRequirements.description:
The pilot project is: aidm-pilot-task-queue
Purpose:
A reliable prioritized in-memory task queue engine supporting:
- FIFO/priority scheduling
- task leasing
- TTL expiration
- deterministic state snapshots
- JSON serialization/deserialization

The eventual pilot is intended to be a small, real, independently versioned TypeScript project.

functionalRequirements.title: Domain Models & Schema Validation
functionalRequirements.description: Type definitions and schema validation for TaskItem, TaskPriority, QueueConfig, and TaskLease.
businessRules: QueueConfig specifies default lease durations, TTL limits, and queue capacities
TaskLease tracks active leases with leaseholder identity and expiration timestamp

functionalRequirements.title: Deterministic State Serialization & Snapshots
functionalRequirements.description: Deterministic JSON state serialization, deserialization, and schema validation of queue state snapshots.
businessRules: Deserialization validates state against schema before restoring in-memory queue
JSON serialization must be strictly deterministic (reproducible ordering)

functionalRequirements.title: Prioritized In-Memory Queue Operations
functionalRequirements.description: Queue operations including enqueue, dequeue, peek, lease, release, and expireStale.
businessRules: FIFO ordering strictly enforced within the same TaskPriority level
Leased tasks are hidden from dequeue until released or expired
expireStale reclaims expired leases and evicts TTL-exceeded tasks

performance: Algorithmic complexity verified structurally (O(1) queue head operations, bounded lookup) with 100 percent automated test pass; no synthetic ops/sec or ms latency SLA
reliability: Deterministic state transitions across enqueue, dequeue, lease, release, TTL lifecycle with 0 seconds unhandled state drift and 100 percent automated test pass
security: Isolated in-memory execution with 0 external network ports, runtime schema validation, and malformed state rejection verified by 100 percent automated security test pass
availability: External uptime percentage SLA is NOT_APPLICABLE; synchronous in-process library availability verified through deterministic execution and 100 percent automated test pass
scalability: QueueConfig capacity limits and bounded configuration verified structurally (maxQueueSize >= 1) with 0 external horizontal scaling dependencies
usability: Strongly typed TypeScript API with explicit error contracts verified by strict compilation (0 errors) and 100 percent API contract automated test pass
maintainability: Strict TypeScript compilation under target Node.js LTS environments (Node.js 18, 20, 22) verified by 100 percent automated build and test pass
operationalConstraints: NOT_APPLICABLE (In-memory TypeScript library consumed as an in-process module; 0 seconds external deployment delay; external hosting excluded per Product Owner Decision 1)

compatibilityConstraints: Strict TypeScript compilation under target Node.js LTS environments (Node.js 18, 20, 22) verified by 100 percent automated build and test pass
operationalConstraints: Modular separation of domain models, queue engine, and serialization adapters
Pure in-memory engine, no external network dependencies or external daemon connections

assumptions.statement: Persistence storage expects In-memory data structures with deterministic JSON snapshot serialization/deserialization
